summary: Sneha pitched Dettol antiseptic liquid and the new Dettol handwash. Dr. Mehta ordered 20 antiseptic and 10 handwash for delivery tomorrow. He raised Patanjali price competition and Dettol's lower margin. The order came only after Sneha offered a personal Diwali gift hamper, which is a high-severity inducement breach.
score_reason: An order was secured, but the margin objection was answered with a personal gift hamper (a high-severity inducement flag that caps the score at 40), key messages were thin, and sample quantities were never stated.

coaching.tip: You confirmed the exact quantities and a delivery day back to the customer. That clear close avoids order confusion.

When margin comes up, respond with approved trade schemes or sell-through value (brand trust, faster rotation), never a personal gift. The Diwali hamper offer is a UCPMP inducement breach and should be reported to your manager.
State sample brand and quantity when offering samples. Also take the dilution feedback seriously: share the approved usage guidance or escalate to medical affairs, not just 'I will note that'.

debrief: Hi Sneha, quick note on Mehta Medicals. You walked out with an order of twenty Dettol antiseptic and ten handwash, and confirmed delivery for tomorrow, which was crisp. One important thing: the Diwali gift hamper offer counts as a personal inducement and breaks our compliance rules, so please don't repeat it; answer margin worries with approved schemes instead. Next, make sure tomorrow's delivery lands and pass on the dilution feedback to the team.
